authored_by: main-session; every number below measured from on-disk artifacts and a live Elasticsearch query in this session
purpose: Decide whether the technical-documentation retrieval corpus may emit a RELEASE report, and refuse to emit scores when it may not. A release report that scores an inadequate golden set is worse than no report: it launders exploratory numbers into evidence.
status_note: Evidence qualifiers such as MODEL_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED are labels only and never promote to VERIFIED (design map line 921).

provenance.note: Measured 2026-08-10 from data/eval/techdocs/qrels.sol-review.jsonl (180 rows) and index knowledge_base_v2_bge_m3 (24877 chunks, live query).

section_path_defect.finding: 178 of 180 qrel section_path values do not exist in the ES section_path set of the document the qrel names. 0 of 180 documents are missing from the index, so this is a label defect, not a corpus gap.
section_path_defect.measurement: For each qrel row, all chunks with that document_id were fetched and their section_path tuples compared. EXACT match: 2. Prefix match: 0. Absent: 178.
section_path_defect.false_matches: The 2 exact matches are both ['Release Notes'], a generic heading that collides by coincidence. The true informative match rate is 0 of 180.
section_path_defect.root_cause: qrel section_path holds a document title or an invented label (e.g. 'What is a container?'), while the parser records the heading hierarchy below the title (e.g. ['Explanation', 'Containers versus virtual machines (VMs)']). The label 'What is a container?' does exist in the index but inside a DIFFERENT document (content/get-started/workshop/_index.md).
section_path_defect.not_version_skew: The index is homogeneous: one parser_version (native-text-v1), one corpus_generation (techdocs-2026-07-30-v1), one model_version. The mismatch cannot be explained by a re-index.
section_path_defect.consequence: Section-level retrieval metrics are not computable on this golden set. A scorer that prefix-matches section_path scores near zero for structural reasons that have nothing to do with retrieval quality.
section_path_defect.scorer_divergence: orchestrator/eval/runner.py::_key() ignores section_path entirely and is why the existing bake-off reports show plausible numbers; orchestrator/eval/metrics.py prefix-matches section_path and would report near zero on identical data. Two scorers, one corpus, incompatible verdicts.
section_path_defect.resolution: Document-level scoring only, at policy v1. Re-deriving section_path automatically from the index is FORBIDDEN because it would use the retriever to author its own gold labels.

release_eligibility.verdict_is_precomputed_expectation: The implementation must derive this verdict from the gates below at run time, not read it from this field. This field records what the authors measured, so a run that reports RELEASE_ELIGIBLE against this data is a bug in the scorer.

blocking_reasons.detail: 23 of 180 rows (12.8%) passed arbitration; 157 are DISPUTED and never resolved.
All 23 arbitrated rows carry relevance 1.0. With no negative in the golden set, precision and false-positive rate are undefined, not merely noisy.
docker and kubernetes contribute 0 of the 23 arbitrated rows, so no claim may span the 6 declared sources.
All 17 pure-negative rows are DISPUTED and 0 are AI_REVIEWED, so the required false-positive / empty-rate report has no eligible data.
178 of 180 section_path labels do not resolve against the index; section-level metrics are forbidden at v1.

gates.note: Every gate must pass before a RELEASE report may be emitted. A gate that cannot be evaluated is a FAILED gate, never a skipped one.

model_identity.evidence_note: endpoint_host is transport configuration evidence; reported_model, response_id, and system_fingerprint must still come from every provider response body in both passes

gates.require_section_path_resolvable_note: false at v1 because section metrics are forbidden outright; document-level scoring does not depend on section_path. Setting this true in a future version requires re-authored labels, not re-derived ones.

gate_rationale.min_golden_rows: 60 is the smallest set where a 6-source stratification can carry ~10 rows per source. It is a floor, not a target.
gate_rationale.require_negative_in_golden: Without a labelled negative, a retriever that returns something for every query cannot be distinguished from one that is correct.
gate_rationale.max_disputed_fraction: Above 20% unresolved labels the set describes reviewer disagreement more than retrieval quality.

scoring.granularity_locked_reason: section_path is unresolvable for 178 of 180 rows (see section_path_defect)
scoring.eligible_rows_rule: review_status == AI_REVIEWED only. DISPUTED rows are never scored, never averaged, and never counted in a denominator.
scoring.pure_negative_handling: Reported separately as false-positive rate and empty-rate. Pure negatives must NEVER enter the macro-average of a relevance metric: a query with no relevant document scores 0.0 by construction and would silently deflate the mean.
scoring.known_prior_defect: data/eval/techdocs/reports/bm25-report.json scored all 180 rows including 157 DISPUTED, and let the 17 pure negatives score 0.0 inside the macro-average. Those reports are exploratory and are not release evidence.
scoring.bootstrap_note: A CI over 23 all-positive rows is reported only to expose its own width. It does not convert an ineligible set into a releasable one.

forbidden_constructions: emitting any metric value (including 0.0) when a gate fails
scoring DISPUTED rows to reach a larger denominator
including pure negatives in a macro-averaged relevance metric
re-deriving section_path from the index and calling the result gold
reporting a section-level metric at policy v1
treating the AI_REVIEWED subset as a holdout (it is dev; it was scored and reviewed)
marking any row HUMAN_REVIEWED without real human participation
generating a real-person reviewer_hash for an AI review pass
promoting AI_REVIEWED to VERIFIED on the strength of confidence values alone

failure_semantics.condition: policy file absent
policy bytes do not match the recorded sha256 sidecar
policy_version is not a version this code understands
qrels file absent or unreadable
a qrel row lacks review_status, relevance, source_id, or document_id
predictions file absent when a metric is requested
any caller asks for a release metric while a gate fails
failure_semantics.forbidden_fallback: return 0.0, 1.0, None, or an empty report that reads like a measurement

failure_semantics.condition: any caller asks for a section-level metric at policy v1
a pure-negative qid reaches the macro-average of a relevance metric
a DISPUTED row reaches the scorer
any required_bindings entry is absent or empty in the report
the signed canonical run manifest qrels hash differs from the qrels bytes consumed by the reporter
signed predictions contain duplicate query IDs or do not exactly match current qrels membership
either review sidecar differs from current qrels in document_id, section_path, relevance, source_id, language, or query_type
two independent review passes do not preserve provider-reported model, response ID, and immutable revision evidence
failure_semantics.forbidden_fallback: requested model name or caller-supplied verified boolean

failure_semantics.condition: both review passes reuse the same provider response ID
review endpoint host or requested model differs from the versioned golden-review policy
the policy-bound split manifest has no non-empty, hash-bound VERIFIED hidden holdout
failure_semantics.forbidden_fallback: dev resampling, a handwritten non-empty size, or an empty-set hash

failure_semantics.condition: split manifest counts or hashes do not match policy-bound query membership
gates evaluated successfully and at least one failed
failure_semantics.note: This is an honest completed verdict, not an error. It is deliberately NOT exit 1.

exit_codes.0: RELEASE_ELIGIBLE: every gate passed and the report carries all required bindings
exit_codes.2: data fault or contract violation (any raise above); nothing was measured
exit_codes.3: NOT_RELEASE_ELIGIBLE: gates evaluated, at least one failed; no metric emitted
exit_codes.reserved_unused_rationale: In the contamination scanner, exit 1 means the BLOCKING business verdict 'contamination found', so an escaping exception there makes a data fault masquerade as a verdict. E5 leaves 1 unused so a crash can never be read as a release decision: 2 always means 'nothing was measured' and 3 always means 'measured, refused'.
